thread:
support-jen: Anyone else seeing a spike in 502/504s from hosted API? Multiple customers reporting timeouts since ~09:03 UTC. Example: customer 12345 saw /v1/generate return 502 then 504 after ~30s. Request IDs: r-1a2b3c, r-4d5e6f. Logs show cache GET errors followed by DB fallback timeouts.

support-jen: snippet from our logs for r-1a2b3c:
```
2026-03-17T09:03:12Z ERROR cache:get key=auth:token:abc123 err="read tcp 10.0.0.5:6379: i/o timeout"
2026-03-17T09:03:13Z WARN  api:handler request_id=r-1a2b3c backend=kv fallback=db latency=31.2s status=504
```

infra-dan: On it. Checking Redis metrics / client pools. Do we have any alerts firing?

ops-bot: ALERT redis-primary-prod connection_rate=92k/s clients=1100 maxclients=1000 p50=45ms p99=350ms

samir: @infra-dan I see spikes coming from a single tenant doing bulk embeddings. Likely connection storm. Throttling them now and reducing parallelism.

infra-dan: If maxclients is hit we get "ERR max number of clients reached" which bubbles as cache errors -> gateway 5xxs. Will look at slowlog and connection pool health.

irina: Noting auth validations failing as well (some 401s for short windows) — looks like token validation calls hit the same KV and time out. Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/auth/validate
```
The endpoint hangs then returns 502 if KV read errors coincide.

eng-oncall: Quick mitigation proposal: treat KV errors as cache-miss immediately and avoid synchronous DB fallbacks for auth calls. Short term config patch: lower client read timeout and flip CACHE_ERROR_AS_MISS so gateway doesn't block.
```
# temp config to deploy
KV_READ_TIMEOUT_MS=50
KV_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS=5
CACHE_ERROR_AS_MISS=true
```
This should convert the 5xx spike into slightly higher DB load but avoid gateway timeouts.

samir: Rolling a temporary throttle on the embeddings tenant (IP-level) and reducing service-worker pool parallelism from 200 -> 50. Watch metrics for connection_rate and clients.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started canary of api-gateway cfg change (CACHE_ERROR_AS_MISS=true) at 2501234600 — 50% canary.

support-jen: I'll update customers with a status note: we're rolling a fix and throttling a noisy tenant. ETA 15–30m for visible recovery. Also capturing request_ids for credits if SLA breached. Which fields should I include in customer follow-up?

infra-dan: Please include request_id, x-hosted-region, timestamp, and any "kv error" lines from logs. We'll assemble a short RCA after stability. Root cause looks like connection storm + insufficient client pooling on Redis.

samir: Error rate trending down after throttle and canary. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

support-jen: Great — I'll send the customer update and track. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
